title: 120 men held a mountain pass until their last round of ammunition ran out. November 18, 2026.
excerpt: On the 64th anniversary of the Battle of Rezang La, the story of Charlie Company's last stand in Ladakh - and the Param Vir Chakra it earned its commander.
bodyHtml:
120 men held a mountain pass until their last round of ammunition ran out

On November 18, 1962, Charlie Company of the 13th Kumaon Regiment defended Rezang La pass in Ladakh until they had nothing left to fight with. Under Major Shaitan Singh, roughly 120 men held the position against a much larger Chinese force for nearly 18 hours during the Sino-Indian War. Official Indian Army history records only 14 survivors.

It became one of the most storied last-stand battles in Indian military history. Major Shaitan Singh was posthumously awarded the Param Vir Chakra, India's highest military decoration for gallantry. The battle is still studied and commemorated as an example of holding a position at any cost.

Rezang La wasn't a battle India won on paper - but the stand itself became part of what the country points to when it talks about what it's capable of defending.
